full_judgment: 11. This decision finds support in the case of Bhagwandas Vs. Saggan reported is A.I.R. 1965 Rajasthan, 143. Here, the learned Judge alter briefly considering the former two cases, found himself unable to accept what he stated as the extreme posit on that a Magistrate can in no case pass an order of attachment without having the preliminary order served upon the party. He found distinction between the commencement of proceedings under subsection (1) of section 145  Cr.P.C. and the commencement of an expiry contemplated under sub-section (4) of the same section. In his opinion the second proviso as it deals with interim orders has reference only to the commencement of the proceedings and not to the commencement of the enquiry.  There can be no bar to issuing an order under the said proviso after the commencement of the proceeding for, otherwise, "there may conceivably be cases of emergency where it may be dangerous to wait for the formality of serving the preliminary order on the parties before issuing an order of attachment." In appropriate cases, a Magistrate is, therefore competent to issue an order of attachment along with the preliminary order which has not yet been served upon the parties.
